Chapter 10: Practical Tools for Changing Habits and Sustaining Progress
So, you’ve started to recognize some unhelpful habits—great first step! But as you probably know, real change takes more than just awareness. It’s about having the right tools, and a bit of ongoing support to keep you going.
I get it—changing patterns you’ve had for years can feel overwhelming. But here’s the good news: small, steady actions can lead to real, lasting transformation.
There’s a simple framework you can use for changing any habit. Let’s break it down:
First, there’s awareness. Start by noticing when a habit gets triggered. How does it show up for you? Maybe it’s a feeling, a thought, or even something physical.
Next up is intention. Decide what new behavior you want to try instead. It doesn’t have to be big—just something you can actually practice.
Then comes experimentation. Try out your new approach in situations where the stakes are low. Notice what works and what doesn’t. It’s all about learning, not getting it perfect right away.
And don’t forget support. Change is so much easier when you’ve got people cheering you on. Maybe that’s an accountability partner, a mentor, or even a coach.
Want an example? Let’s say you tend to downplay your contributions at work meetings. This time, set an intention to share just one idea per meeting—even if it’s a small one. Or if you find yourself stuck in rumination after something stressful, try out a quick “reset ritual” to help you move on.
These little experiments might seem tiny, but over time, they build your confidence and actually help your brain create new pathways.
Here’s something else to keep in mind: track your progress and celebrate your wins, even the small ones. Change isn’t a straight line—setbacks happen, and that’s totally normal. When you focus on growth instead of perfection, you give yourself room to learn and to keep going, no matter what.
So, remember—lasting change isn’t about doing everything perfectly. It’s about taking small steps, asking for help when you need it, and being kind to yourself along the way.
